items.quote: "Brummie" is also a demonym for people from Birmingham
items.note: Accept 'Brum' for the accent at the host's discretion; 'Brummie' is the standard answer for both.

items.quote: Bournville is a 19th century model village on the southwest side of Birmingham, England, founded by the Quaker Cadbury family for employees at its Cadbury's factory
items.note: Was in northern Worcestershire when founded; now a Birmingham suburb, so the question holds.

items.quote: Birmingham became known as the "City of a thousand trades" because of the wide variety of goods manufactured there
items.note: The phrase is not in en:Birmingham, only in History of Birmingham and Economy of Birmingham. 'Workshop of the World' is a rival nickname, but the question's wording fixes the answer.

items.quote: Black Sabbath were an English heavy metal band formed in Birmingham in 1968
items.note: Question gives a lot away (year, Ozzy); fine for a family round.

items.quote: it follows the exploits of the Peaky Blinders crime gang in the direct aftermath of the First World War
A region of Birmingham with many balti restaurants has become known as the Balti Triangle
items.note: Answer is right, but the premise 'named after the steel pan' is disputed: the article's Origin section gives a rival derivation from Baltistan (Pat Chapman) against the cooking-pot one (Colleen Taylor Sen). Suggested rewording: 'Which curry, served in a thin steel bowl of the same name, was developed in Birmingham in the 1970s?'

items.quote: Aston Villa defeated Bundesliga winners Bayern Munich 1-0 at De Kuip in Rotterdam
Tolkien's mother took him to live with her parents in Kings Heath, Birmingham
items.note: Born in Bloemfontein, South Africa (1892), so 'childhood' not 'born' is the right wording, as written.

items.quote: UB40 recorded a cover version in 1983 for their album Labour of Love
items.note: UK number one in 1983 per en:UB40. Neil Diamond wrote it, but the question asks for the Birmingham band.
